public_rationale: This is an open-ended forecast with no deadline. A US federal advisory reported in August 2026 already described attackers using AI-made scripts against energy and water controllers. That fits the forecast's direction, but it came before the post, so it cannot count as the outcome. After the post, I found only a Trend Micro warning that AI is probably behind attacks on Japanese firms, including financial services. The AI use there is inferred, not confirmed. No readable post-dated official report clearly documents AI-assisted attacks on financial systems, rail or power. The forecast stays open.
limitations: Several October 2026 reports could not be read.
Pre-post evidence suggests the behaviour was already under way, which a reader might see as near-confirmation, but it falls outside the forecast window.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Malicious actors will try to use current AI to undermine financial systems and vital infrastructure like trains and electrical systems.

statement.excerpt: We should expect that malicious actors will try use current AI to undermine financial systems and other vital infrastructure such as trains or electrical systems.

from_speaker: other vital infrastructure such as trains or electrical systems
our_interpretation: Read as a forecast that, after the post, malicious actors (criminals or state hackers) will be documented trying to use AI tools available around the time of the post to attack or disrupt financial systems or critical infrastructure such as rail, power or similar utilities.
'Try' means an attempt is enough; the attack does not need to succeed.
No deadline is given, so the forecast is open-ended.
criteria.support_condition: A credible government advisory, official investigation, or security-firm report, dated after 2026-09-21, documents malicious actors using AI tools to attack or attempt to attack financial systems or vital infrastructure such as rail, power, water or similar.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An open-ended 'will try' forecast cannot be firmly contradicted by an absence of reports. It would be weakened only if, over a long period, official reviews found no AI-assisted attempts against such systems.
